\section*{Question 6}

Consider the curve given by the equation \(y^{3}-x y=2\). It can be shown that \(\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{y}{3 y^{2}-x}\).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Write an equation for the line tangent to the curve at the point \((-1,1)\).
\item[(b)] Find the coordinates of all points on the curve at which the line tangent to the curve at that point is vertical.
\item[(c)] Evaluate \(\frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}}\) at the point on the curve where \(x=-1\) and \(y=1\).
\item[(a)] \(\left.\frac{d y}{d x}\right|_{(x, y)=(-1,1)}=\frac{1}{3(1)^{2}-(-1)}=\frac{1}{4}\)
An equation for the tangent line is \(y=\frac{1}{4}(x+1)+1\).
\item[(b)] \(3 y^{2}-x=0 \Rightarrow x=3 y^{2}\)
So, \(y^{3}-x y=2 \Rightarrow y^{3}-\left(3 y^{2}\right)(y)=2 \Rightarrow y=-1\)
\[
(-1)^{3}-x(-1)=2 \Rightarrow x=3
\]
The tangent line to the curve is vertical at the point (3, -1).
\end{itemize}
\(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { slope } \\ 1: \text { equation for tangent line }\end{array}\right.\)
\(3:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { sets } 3 y^{2}-x=0 \\ 1: \text { equation in one variable } \\ 1: \text { coordinates }\end{array}\right.\)
\begin{itemize}
\item[(c)] \(\frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}}=\frac{\left(3 y^{2}-x\right) \frac{d y}{d x}-y\left(6 y \frac{d y}{d x}-1\right)}{\left(3 y^{2}-x\right)^{2}}\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
\left.\frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}}\right|_{(x, y)=(-1,1)} & =\frac{\left(3 \cdot 1^{2}-(-1)\right) \cdot \frac{1}{4}-1 \cdot\left(6 \cdot 1 \cdot \frac{1}{4}-1\right)}{\left(3 \cdot 1^{2}-(-1)\right)^{2}} \\
& =\frac{1-\frac{1}{2}}{16}=\frac{1}{32}
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{itemize}
4 : \(\left\{\begin{array}{l}2 \text { : implicit differentiation } \\ 1: \text { substitution for } \frac{d y}{d x} \\ 1: \text { answer }\end{array}\right.\)
